<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919688_theRebbe_695" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919688_theRebbe_695__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Devarim,</t>
    <t s="2">Shabbat Chazon,</t>
    <t s="3">5735*.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "Tzion" refers to the innerness of the heart, which is redeemed through Torah, while the captive powers are redeemed specifically through charity.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh v'shaveha b'tzedakah"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and the Alter Rebbe2 explains</t>
    <t s="2">and the Tzemach Tzedek3</t>
    <t s="3">(and our Nesi'im who followed),</t>
    <t s="4">that Tzion refers to the aspect of the innerness of the heart.</t>
    <t s="5">And it is called Tzion, a term for a sign,</t>
    <t s="6">because the aspect of the innerness of the heart is a sign and marker for that which is above.</t>
    <t s="7">And in this aspect, it is impossible for there to be captivity, G-d forbid,</t>
    <t s="8">rather it only requires redemption,</t>
    <t s="9">and the redemption is through mishpat, meaning Torah,</t>
    <t s="10">as its Targum [translates] "according to the first judgment"4</t>
    <t s="11">"as the first law."</t>
    <t s="12">And "shaveha" (her captives) are the revealed powers of the soul that are in the aspect of enclothing in the body,</t>
    <t s="13">the aspect of the "leg" of the soul,</t>
    <t s="14">which are in a state of actual captivity,</t>
    <t s="15">and their redemption from captivity is specifically through tzedakah,</t>
    <t s="16">which is the performance of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="17">as explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="18">(in the discourse "Tzion b'mishpat"5)</t>
    <t s="19">at length.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section presents a second interpretation that "shaveha" refers to bringing righteous ones to repentance, which is a higher level accomplished through tzedakah and specifically by Mashiach, who possesses the level of Yechidah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">1)</t>
    <t s="1">2)</t>
    <t s="2">Now, according to this explanation,</t>
    <t s="3">"Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh"</t>
    <t s="4">(redemption through Torah)</t>
    <t s="5">is higher than "shaveha b'tzedakah"</t>
    <t s="6">(redemption through mitzvos),</t>
    <t s="7">and consistent with what is explained in many places that Torah is higher than mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="8">However, in the Reshimot of the Tzemach Tzedek on the Prophets and Writings6,</t>
    <t s="9">on the verse "Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh v'shaveha b'tzedakah",</t>
    <t s="10">he brings an explanation,</t>
    <t s="11">that "shaveha" is the matter of bringing righteous ones to repentance.</t>
    <t s="12">For Tzion refers to the righteous7,</t>
    <t s="13">and the "captives" of Tzion are the matter of bringing righteous ones to repentance8,</t>
    <t s="14">and the redemption of the righteous is through the Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">but bringing righteous ones to repentance is accomplished specifically through tzedakah.</t>
    <t s="16">And according to this explanation, "v'shaveha b'tzedakah" is higher than "Tzion b'mishpat tipadeh",</t>
    <t s="17">and moreover, it is an incomparably greater elevation.</t>
    <t s="18">And this is also understood from the fact that bringing righteous ones to repentance is specifically through Mashiach,</t>
    <t s="19">as per the statement9</t>
    <t s="20">"Mashiach has come to bring righteous ones to repentance",</t>
    <t s="21">for the level of the soul of Mashiach is incomparable to the levels of other souls,</t>
    <t s="22">as is known in the writings of the Arizal10,</t>
    <t s="23">that the level of soul that the great ones of Israel merited until Mashiach is only in the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and Chayah,</t>
    <t s="24">and Adam HaRishon merited Chayah,</t>
    <t s="25">but Mashiach will merit Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="26">the general Yechidah of all of Israel.</t>
    <t s="27">And the elevation of the aspect of Yechidah over the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and Chayah is an incomparable elevation.</t>
    <t s="28">And this is also understood from the fact that it is called Yechidah, from the word Yachid (singular),</t>
    <t s="29">a term which indicates that it has no comparison to the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and Chayah.</t>
    <t s="30">And as is known11</t>
    <t s="31">the difference between Yachid and Echad,</t>
    <t s="32">for Echad indicates that it has a relation to another thing</t>
    <t s="33">[for although the term Echad is not like the term Rishon (first),</t>
    <t s="34">for Rishon necessitates that there is a second,</t>
    <t s="35">unlike Echad, for there is one and no second to it12,</t>
    <t s="36">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="37">from the very fact that it is necessary to say "and no second", it proves that a second to it could possibly exist,</t>
    <t s="38">in relation to it, etc.],</t>
    <t s="39">but the term Yachid,</t>
    <t s="40">this itself indicates that there is no second to it.</t>
    <t s="41">And from this the magnitude of the elevation of bringing righteous ones to repentance is understood,</t>
    <t s="42">since this is one of the matters that will be innovated specifically by Mashiach,</t>
    <t s="43">the aspect of Yechidah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
